questions.explanation: Mission-mode administration organises a programme around clearly defined goals, timelines, leadership, resources, measurable milestones and monitoring mechanisms to achieve specific public outcomes.

questions.subject: Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Sevottam model?

options.A: A framework for improving public service delivery through three interconnected elements: effective Citizen's Charters, effective public grievance redressal and excellence in service delivery capability

questions.explanation: Sevottam is a framework for improving public service delivery through three interconnected elements: effective Citizen's Charters, effective public grievance redressal and excellence in service delivery capability.
questions.source: Public Administration Notes, Section J and Section K

questions.subject: Public Administration
questions.question: What are the three broad components of the Sevottam model?

options.A: Citizen's Charters, public grievance redressal and service delivery capability

questions.explanation: The three broad components of Sevottam are Citizen's Charters, public grievance redressal and service delivery capability.

questions.subject: Public Administration
questions.question: What is the role of capacity building in administrative reform?

options.A: Capacity building develops the knowledge, skills, attitudes, leadership and institutional systems required for public servants to perform effectively
options.B: Capacity building refers to constructing new office buildings
options.C: Capacity building refers to increasing the number of government holidays
options.D: Capacity building refers to reducing the number of public servants

questions.explanation: Capacity building develops the knowledge, skills, attitudes, leadership and institutional systems required for public servants to perform effectively. It includes training, competency frameworks, learning systems and performance support.

questions.subject: Public Administration
questions.question: What is Mission Karmayogi?

options.A: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building launched in 2020 to move civil-service capacity building towards a role-based, competency-driven and continuous learning approach
options.B: A programme to construct new Parliament buildings
options.C: A scheme for providing pensions to civil servants
options.D: A programme to reduce the number of civil servants

questions.explanation: Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, was launched in 2020 to move civil-service capacity building towards a role-based, competency-driven and continuous learning approach. The iGOT Karmayogi digital platform supports learning and capacity development.

questions.subject: Public Administration
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Right to Public Services approach?

options.A: To make specified public services available within notified time limits and provide accountability or remedies for delay or denial, with States enacting service-guarantee laws
options.C: To make public services available only to government employees
options.D: To remove all time limits for public services

questions.explanation: The Right to Public Services approach seeks to make specified public services available within notified time limits and provide accountability or remedies for delay or denial. States have enacted service-guarantee laws; Karnataka's Sakala framework is an example.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Max Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy?

options.A: Recruitment based on family lineage

questions.explanation: Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy features recruitment based on technical qualifications, not family lineage. Other features include clear hierarchy, written rules and records, specialisation, career service, separation of official position from personal ownership and impersonal rule-based decision-making.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an exemption under Section 8 of the RTI Act?

options.A: Information relating to government expenditure on welfare schemes
options.D: Cabinet papers subject to statutory conditions

questions.explanation: Information relating to government expenditure on welfare schemes is generally not exempt; exemptions under Section 8 include information affecting sovereignty and security, information forbidden by a court, parliamentary privilege, commercial confidence, fiduciary information, foreign government confidences, information endangering life or safety, investigation-related information, Cabinet papers and personal information as amended.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stage of an effective grievance redressal system?

options.A: Destroying complaints without recording them

questions.explanation: An effective grievance redressal system includes accessible complaint registration, acknowledgement and tracking, assignment to a responsible authority, investigation, time-bound decision, communication of reasons and outcome, appeal or review where available and analysis of recurring complaints. Destroying complaints is not a stage.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a commonly recognised principle of good governance?

options.A: Arbitrary rule

questions.explanation: Commonly recognised principles of good governance include participation, rule of law, transparency, responsiveness, consensus orientation, equity and inclusiveness, effectiveness and efficiency, accountability and strategic vision. Arbitrary rule is the opposite of good governance.

questions.chapter: Quick Revision - Concepts and Statutory References
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of e-governance?

options.A: Increased physical paperwork

questions.explanation: Benefits of e-governance include reduced transaction time and costs, improved access to information, standardised procedures, online applications and payments, digital records, improved tracking and data-informed decisions. Increased physical paperwork is not a benefit.

questions.subject: Public Administration

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of excessive hierarchy?

options.A: Improved speed of decision-making

questions.explanation: Limitations of excessive hierarchy include delays, rigid procedures, communication distortion, excessive centralisation, reluctance to take initiative and distance between senior decision-makers and citizens. Improved speed of decision-making is not a limitation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method of administrative coordination?

options.A: Maintaining complete secrecy between departments

questions.explanation: Methods of administrative coordination include Cabinet and committee systems, inter-departmental meetings, nodal departments, common guidelines, joint task forces, shared databases, integrated plans and budgets, review mechanisms and clearly assigned lead agencies. Maintaining secrecy between departments is not a coordination method.

questions.subject: Public Administration

questions.chapter: Quick Revision - Concepts and Statutory References
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major form of public accountability?

options.A: Accountability to foreign governments
options.D: Social accountability through citizens and media

questions.explanation: Major forms of public accountability include political accountability to elected representatives, administrative accountability through supervision, legal accountability through courts, financial accountability through audit and legislative committees, and social accountability through citizens, media, public hearings and community monitoring. Accountability to foreign governments is not a major form in the notes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Right to Information Act, 2005?

options.A: It requires the PIO to create new information on request
options.B: It provides access to information held by public authorities
options.C: It provides for first and second appeals
options.D: It provides for penalties on PIOs for delay

questions.explanation: The RTI Act provides access to information that exists and is held by or under the control of a public authority. A PIO is not generally required to create new information, conduct research, draw inferences or provide explanations not held on record.

Increasing compliance burden is not a reform area.

questions.subject: Public Administration
questions.topic: Quick Revision - Concepts and Statutory References
questions.chapter: Quick Revision - Concepts and Statutory References
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a difference between Public Administration and Private Administration?

options.A: Public Administration is always illegal, while Private Administration is always legal
options.B: Public Administration operates primarily for public interest, while Private Administration generally operates for commercial objectives
options.C: Public Administration is accountable to citizens and elected institutions, while Private Administration is accountable to private owners
options.D: Public Administration is subject to constitutional and legal controls, while Private Administration operates within private ownership

questions.explanation: Public Administration operates primarily for public interest, is subject to constitutional and legal controls and is accountable to citizens and elected institutions. Private Administration generally operates within private ownership and commercial objectives. The statement that Public Administration is always illegal is incorrect.
